the ask, verbatim
Produce ONE v2-format test edition through the paper's full pipeline: three independent drafts, one selection, one adversarial review. The edition spec every draft must follow in full: Produce today's TEST EDITION of Open Interest's daily crypto brief, format v2: a NEWSPAPER, not a research digest. Plain text only, under 1,700 words. Quality of news judgment, voice and sourcing is the entire point. FIRST: fetch and obey the house style guide at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openinterest-ai/paper/main/style-guide.html (binding: declarative sentences, numbers with context, banned words, at most one em dash PER STORY, absolute dates, no financial advice). Cite with the full source URL in square brackets. STRUCTURE (exactly): LEAD: the day's single most consequential story, ANY category - an exploit, a ruling, an upgrade, a collapse. Declarative headline ending in a full stop, a 2-sentence deck, then 200-300 words, every claim sourced. NEWS - exactly three items: EVENTS. Hacks and exploits, regulation and enforcement, exchanges and companies, market-structure events. Never price commentary. Tag [NEWS], declarative headline with full stop, 3-4 sentences, at least one source URL each. TECH - exactly two items: protocols, research, engineering. Tag [TECH], same shape. CULTURE - exactly two items: governance fights, community conflicts, narratives, the people and institutions of the discourse. Tag [CULTURE], same shape. READING LIST: 3-5 links, each with a 1-line reason. METHOD: one closing paragraph: sources swept, hours covered, items cut for failed verification, claims resting on secondary sources. SOURCES - the roster and the record: - The paper's masthead (88 voices): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openinterest-ai/paper/main/masthead/voices.csv - prefer these voices' own writing for TECH and CULTURE. - NEWS events may rest on: official announcements, status pages and company blogs; ON-CHAIN EVIDENCE and analytics investigations (cite transactions and addresses where material); court and regulator documents; and reputable secondary reporting ATTRIBUTED BY NAME where no primary source exists - never stated as bare fact, always disclosed in METHOD. - X only via open mirrors. Prefer the last 24-48 hours. - A claim that cannot be verified is cut, and the cut is noted in METHOD. When sources conflict on a figure, prefer the primary source; otherwise state the range and attribute both. CONTINUITY: before drafting, fetch https://openinterest-ai.github.io/paper/rehearsal.html and the prior test editions linked there. Do NOT lead with a story a prior edition led with unless a material NEW development happened after it. ACCEPTANCE: the structure above complete with EXACT section counts; every claim sourced; under 1,700 words; no banned words; headlines are declarative sentences with full stops; absolute dates only; at most one em dash per story.
